note: Rewritten from Wasmann's Latin original description of 1902 (new species Amitermes Foreli n. sp.), which describes only the soldier (Miles); type locality Colombia. The antennal segment count in the original is OCR-damaged (given as "44-vel 12-articulatae", presumably 11 or 12 segments), so this entry gives no segment count. The end of the original also cites Silvestri 1901, Bollettino dei Musei di Zoologia ed Anatomia comparata della R. Università di Torino 16(389).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier: body length 6—6.5 mm, head including mandibles 2.5 mm; the whole body white, the head white-yellow; head large, globose, strongly convex, strongly rounded behind, narrowing in front, slightly longer than wide; frons without spines, grooved in front; mandibles about half the head length, jet black at the apex, stout, strongly curved, each with a tooth before the middle.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Body length 6—6.5 mm; head including mandibles 2.5 mm. Body white, head white-yellow. Head large, globose, very convex, very rounded behind, narrowing in front, only slightly longer than wide. Antennal segments distinctly lengthening towards the apex, the fourth segment from the apex twice as long as wide or more, the terminal segment 4 times as long as wide and longer than the preceding segment. Frons without spines, grooved in front. Mandibles about half the head length, jet black at the apex, stout, strongly curved, each with a tooth before the middle of the mandible. Labrum oval, not reaching the middle of the mandibles, only slightly longer than wide, narrowing and pointed towards the apex. Pronotum small, almost hidden by the head, more than one times narrower than the head, transverse.
